metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Morris County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Newark Pompton & Riverdale Rd District, Hamburg Turnpike & Post Lane Hills
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 2.64%, with an equalization ratio of 82.5%.
Public education represents 61.5% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 28.5%.
Average residential assessment is $379,500, producing an average annual tax bill of $10,018.8.

neighborhoods.name: Newark Pompton & Riverdale Rd District
neighborhoods.character: Cozy single-family homes, modern townhome developments, and Route 23 retail corridor along Pequannock River
neighborhoods.description: Compact borough convenient to Route 23 shopping, Route 287, and commuter buses to NYC.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Major commercial shopping centers on Route 23 provide a substantial ratable cushion.

neighborhoods.name: Hamburg Turnpike & Post Lane Hills
neighborhoods.character: Elevated residential neighborhood near Pequannock border with custom single-family homes and modern townhouses
neighborhoods.description: Sought-after residential pocket convenient to Route 23 corridor and Pompton Lake.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Benefits from commercial ratable contributions along Route 23 retail zone.

equityAnalysis.summary: Riverdale Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Riverdale Borough, homeowners pay an average of $10,018.8 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 9.07% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 82.5%, assessed values average ~82.5% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 61.5% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 28.5%, and Morris County claims 10.0%.
